name: Capture attribute (camera or mic from a file input)
plain: Opens the phone camera or microphone directly from a file input; the page gets one finished file.
meaning: A site can skip the gallery and ask for a fresh photo, video or recording. It gets a single file, not a live stream, and the person confirms each capture.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
steps: Camera or voice recorder app opens
Person captures and confirms; File returns to the page

chrome.note: Desktop falls back to the file chooser

edge.note: Desktop falls back to the file chooser

firefox.note: Desktop falls back to the file chooser

safari.note: Desktop falls back to the file chooser

limits.headline: Can open your camera or microphone app for one photo, video or clip
limits.user_action: You tap Take photo, Scan document or Record video on an upload button.
can: Start the phone's camera app straight from an upload button
Ask for the front or back camera
cannot: Take extra pictures after the first
See your photo library, only the one new picture
Work on computers, which show a normal file chooser
limits.differs: Works on iPhone and Android phones. Desktop browsers ignore it and show the usual file chooser.

story.what_it_is: A file button that opens your phone camera or microphone directly and hands over one finished file.

marketing.name: HTML capture attribute
marketing.pitch: Documents a tag that asks a phone to open the camera or recorder to fill a file field.

story.for_you: You tap 'Take photo' and your phone camera opens. You shoot, accept, and the page gets just that one picture. It never sees a live camera feed.
story.for_makers: It is the simplest way to collect a photo or clip with no camera code and no permission fuss. Makers use it for ID checks, claims and listings. The person picks what to send.

use_cases.example: A bank asks you to photograph your ID and a cheque, then uploads both with one tap.
A marketplace lets you snap photos of an item to sell right from the listing form.
A clinic portal lets you take a photo of a rash for the nurse to see.
A homework site lets students photograph their work and submit it.
A delivery site asks for a photo of a damaged package.
A site lets you record a short voice or video note straight into a post.
A field service app records a photo of a repair as proof of work.

technical_bounds: Mobile only effect: desktop browsers fall back to the file chooser
Values user (front camera) or environment (rear camera); the app may let the person switch
Result is a single file; the page cannot stream or preview before the capture ends
Combined with accept=image/*, video/* or audio/* to choose the capture type
No separate camera permission prompt on most browsers because the OS camera app does the capture

abuse: Pushing people to take photos of sensitive documents

history.change: capture attribute supported in iOS Safari (BCD)
